questions.sec: Ciliopathy overview: cilia function & types · p786
questions.q: Ciliopathies are best defined as:
opts: Hereditary cystic disorders of the kidney caused by a tubular epithelium defect
Acquired cystic diseases of the kidney arising after middle age
Glomerular diseases due to podocyte injury
questions.exp: Ciliopathies are hereditary cystic disorders of the kidney: cilia maintain the differentiated phenotype of tubular epithelium, and a defect causes cysts. (Book p786)

questions.sec: Ciliopathy overview: cilia function & types · p786
questions.q: Fill up: Cilia maintain the differentiated phenotype of ______ epithelium.
questions.exp: Cilia function: maintain the differentiated phenotype of tubular epithelium, and this function is regulated by polycystin. (Book p786)

questions.sec: Ciliopathy overview: cilia function & types · p786
questions.q: A defect in the cilia of renal tubular epithelium leads to which structural consequence?
opts: Loss of the differentiated phenotype with cyst formation
Diffuse thickening of the glomerular basement membrane
Thrombotic microangiopathy with fragmented red cells
questions.exp: Defect of cilia → ciliopathies: the tubular epithelium loses its differentiated phenotype and cysts develop. (Book p786)

questions.sec: Ciliopathy overview: cilia function & types · p786
questions.q: The function of cilia in tubular epithelium is regulated by:
questions.exp: Cilia function — maintaining the differentiated phenotype of tubular epithelium — is regulated by polycystin. (Book p786)

questions.sec: Ciliopathy overview: cilia function & types · p786
questions.q: Match the four types in the ciliopathy flowchart — 1) ADPKD  2) ARPKD  3) Juvenile nephronophthisis  4) MCDK … A) Medullary cystic disease of kidney  B) Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease  C) Autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease  D) Juvenile nephronophthisis
questions.exp: The TYPES flowchart lists four ciliopathies: ADPKD, ARPKD, juvenile nephronophthisis and medullary cystic disease of kidney (MCDK). (Book p786)

questions.sec: Ciliopathy overview: cilia function & types · p786
questions.q: Which entity is NOT one of the four ciliopathies listed in the TYPES flowchart?
questions.exp: Medullary sponge kidney is later described as 'not a ciliopathy' — an acquired disease; the four ciliopathies listed are ADPKD, ARPKD, juvenile nephronophthisis and MCDK. (Book p786)

questions.sec: ADPKD: features, genes, Ravinson's criteria · p786
questions.q: Regarding ADPKD, which statement is correct?
opts: Autosomal dominant with variable expression, so few develop ESRD
Autosomal recessive, with ESRD in all patients by 40 years
Autosomal dominant with no spontaneous mutations
Autosomal recessive with only 5% of nephrons involved
questions.exp: ADPKD: autosomal dominant with variable expression (few develop ESRD), 10% due to spontaneous mutation, multiple bilateral renal cysts as hallmark, and only 5% of nephrons involved. (Book p786)

questions.sec: ADPKD: features, genes, Ravinson's criteria · p786
questions.q: What percentage of ADPKD is due to spontaneous (new) mutation?
questions.exp: ADPKD: 10% is due to spontaneous mutation (no family history). (Book p786)

questions.sec: ADPKD: features, genes, Ravinson's criteria · p786
questions.q: Fill up: In ADPKD, only ______% of nephrons are involved, so renal function is preserved for long.
questions.exp: ADPKD involves only 5% of nephrons — hence preserved renal function despite massive cystic kidneys. (Book p786)

questions.sec: ADPKD: features, genes, Ravinson's criteria · p786
questions.q: Multiple bilateral renal cysts are the hallmark of ADPKD.
opts: False — the hallmark is a single cyst per kidney
False — the hallmark is medullary nephrocalcinosis
questions.exp: Hallmark of ADPKD: multiple bilateral renal cysts; genes PKD1 (85%) and PKD2 (15%). (Book p786)

questions.sec: ADPKD: features, genes, Ravinson's criteria · p786
questions.q: Match the ADPKD gene with its chromosome and product — 1) PKD1  2) PKD2 … A) Chr4q — polycystin 2, milder disease  B) Chr16p — polycystin 1, 85% of cases
questions.exp: Gene defect in ADPKD: PKD1 on Chr16p (85%) → polycystin 1; PKD2 on Chr4q (15%) → polycystin 2 (milder disease); PKD3 (GANA B). (Book p786)

questions.sec: ADPKD: features, genes, Ravinson's criteria · p786
questions.q: PKD1 on chromosome 16p accounts for what percentage of ADPKD?
questions.exp: PKD1 (Chr16p → polycystin 1) accounts for 85%; PKD2 (Chr4q → polycystin 2) accounts for 15% and causes milder disease. (Book p786)

questions.sec: ADPKD: features, genes, Ravinson's criteria · p786
questions.q: A patient with ADPKD has a PKD2 mutation. Compared with PKD1 disease, the expected course is:
opts: More severe disease with earlier ESRD
questions.exp: PKD2 (Chr4q → polycystin 2) produces milder disease than PKD1, which accounts for 85% of cases. (Book p786)

questions.sec: ADPKD: features, genes, Ravinson's criteria · p786
questions.q: Why is hypertension so common in ADPKD, even early in the disease?
opts: Polycystin is also present in vascular smooth muscle
Renin secretion is switched off by the cysts
Sodium is lost in the urine because of tubular damage
Cardiac output is reduced by pericardial involvement
questions.exp: The boxed note: polycystin is also present in vascular smooth muscle, and hence in ADPKD hypertension is present. (Book p786)

questions.sec: ADPKD: features, genes, Ravinson's criteria · p786
questions.q: The polycystin protein of ADPKD is expressed in vascular smooth muscle, which helps explain the hypertension of ADPKD.
opts: False — polycystin is restricted to tubular epithelium
False — the hypertension of ADPKD is due to anaemia
True, but only in PKD2 disease
questions.exp: Boxed note: polycystin is also present in vascular smooth muscle → in ADPKD, HTN is present. (Book p786)

questions.sec: ADPKD: features, genes, Ravinson's criteria · p786
questions.q: Match the Ravinson's criteria age band with the number of cysts needed for diagnosis of ADPKD — 1) 15–39 years  2) 40–59 years  3) ≥60 years … A) ≥2 cysts bilaterally  B) ≥3 cysts (unilateral or bilateral)  C) ≥4 cysts bilaterally
questions.exp: Ravinson's criteria (based on USG, the investigation of choice): 15–39 years — ≥3 cysts (u/l or b/l); 40–59 years — ≥2 cysts bilaterally; ≥60 years — ≥4 cysts bilaterally. (Book p786)

questions.sec: ADPKD: features, genes, Ravinson's criteria · p786
questions.q: Fill up: The diagnostic criteria for ADPKD (Ravinson's criteria) are based on ______, which is the investigation of choice.
questions.exp: Ravinson's criteria for ADPKD diagnosis are based on USG, marked as the investigation of choice (IOC). (Book p786)

questions.sec: ADPKD: features, genes, Ravinson's criteria · p786
questions.q: A 45-year-old with a family history of ADPKD needs how many cysts on ultrasound to satisfy Ravinson's criteria?
opts: Only one cyst in either kidney
questions.exp: For ages 40–59 years the criterion is ≥2 cysts bilaterally (≥3 cysts u/l or b/l applies at 15–39 years, and ≥4 bilaterally at ≥60 years). (Book p786)

questions.sec: ADPKD: features, genes, Ravinson's criteria · p786
questions.q: A 66-year-old woman with a family history of ADPKD has a renal ultrasound. How many cysts bilaterally are required by Ravinson's criteria?
questions.exp: For age ≥60 years, Ravinson's criteria require ≥4 cysts bilaterally. (Book p786)

questions.sec: ADPKD: features, genes, Ravinson's criteria · p786
questions.q: All but one of the following are correct Ravinson's criteria pairings. Which is the odd one out?
questions.exp: In the 15–39 year band the requirement is ≥3 cysts (unilateral or bilateral), not ≥2 bilaterally (which is the 40–59 year rule). (Book p786)

questions.sec: ADPKD: features, genes, Ravinson's criteria · p786
questions.q: The gross specimen figure labelled 'cysts in ADPKD' shows kidneys in which the external and cut surfaces demonstrate:
opts: Multiple cysts of varying size replacing normal parenchyma
Uniformly small kidneys with cortical scarring
Dilated spongy medullary collecting ducts without macrocysts
questions.exp: The figure of ADPKD (external and cut surface) shows multiple cysts of varying size in both kidneys, the hallmark of the disease. (Book p786)

questions.sec: ADPKD clinical features & anaemia note · p787
questions.q: A 28-year-old man is found to have bilateral enlarged cystic kidneys during an ultrasound performed because his father has ADPKD. He has no complaints. This presentation is:
opts: The commonest presentation — asymptomatic, diagnosed incidentally or on family screening
A rare presentation — most patients with ADPKD present with uraemic symptoms
A presentation typical of ARPKD that is being diagnosed first in adulthood
A presentation diagnostic of acquired medullary sponge kidney disease
questions.exp: ADPKD clinical features begin with 'Asymptomatic: m/c presentation' — incidental diagnosis or USG done because of family history. (Book p787)

questions.sec: ADPKD clinical features & anaemia note · p787
questions.q: Abdominal discomfort in ADPKD usually occurs at what age?
questions.exp: Abdominal discomfort usually at 30–40 years, due to renomegaly (can have abdominal distension). (Book p787)

questions.sec: ADPKD clinical features & anaemia note · p787
questions.q: Fill up: Abdominal discomfort in ADPKD is caused by ______.
questions.exp: Abdominal discomfort in ADPKD (usually at 30–40 years) is due to renomegaly, which can produce abdominal distension. (Book p787)

questions.sec: ADPKD clinical features & anaemia note · p787
questions.q: Hypertension in ADPKD is important because it:
opts: Can lead to severe target organ damage
Is always a late feature after ESRD
questions.exp: Clinical feature 3: HTN in ADPKD can lead to severe target organ damage. (Book p787)

questions.sec: ADPKD clinical features & anaemia note · p787
questions.q: A patient with ADPKD reports that he wakes up twice a night to pass urine, whereas previously he passed urine 3 times in a day and once at night. This nocturia indicates:
opts: Tubular involvement with impaired concentrating capacity
Bladder outflow obstruction from a pelvic cyst
questions.exp: Nocturia — a change in the day-to-night frequency of urination (normal: 3 times in day, 1 at night) — results from tubular involvement and impaired concentrating capacity. (Book p787)

questions.sec: ADPKD clinical features & anaemia note · p787
questions.q: Fill up: Normal urinary frequency is ______ times in the day and one at night.
questions.exp: The nocturia note records normal frequency as 3 times in the day and 1 time at night; a change in this ratio is nocturia due to impaired concentrating ability. (Book p787)

questions.sec: ADPKD clinical features & anaemia note · p787
questions.q: Match the ADPKD symptoms with their mechanisms — 1) Nocturia and polyuria  2) Anaemia … A) Less common because EPO production is preserved  B) Tubular involvement with impaired concentrating capacity
questions.exp: Nocturia and polyuria are due to tubular involvement → impaired concentrating capacity; anaemia is less common because EPO production is preserved. (Book p787)

questions.sec: ADPKD clinical features & anaemia note · p787
questions.q: Anaemia is less common in ADPKD because EPO production is preserved.
opts: False — anaemia is universal in ADPKD
False — EPO production rises in ADPKD
True only after dialysis is started
questions.exp: Clinical feature 6 in ADPKD: anaemia is less common due to preserved EPO production. (Book p787)

questions.sec: ADPKD clinical features & anaemia note · p787
questions.q: Among the CKD conditions listed, which has the least anaemia?
questions.exp: Note: CKD with least anaemia — ADPKD, because EPO production is preserved. (Book p787)

questions.sec: ADPKD clinical features & anaemia note · p787
questions.q: All but one of the following are listed clinical features of ADPKD. Which is the odd one out?
questions.exp: ADPKD is remarkable for the least anaemia among CKD causes (EPO is preserved); the other items are listed features. (Book p787)

questions.sec: ADPKD complications & renal stone types · p787
questions.q: What percentage of ADPKD patients develop ESRD by 60 years?
questions.exp: Complication: ESRD — only 60% develop ESRD by 60 years, reflecting the variable expression of ADPKD. (Book p787)

questions.sec: ADPKD complications & renal stone types · p787
questions.q: Match each indicator of bad prognosis in ADPKD with its description — 1) Black males  2) Diagnosis before 30 years  3) Hematuria at presentation  4) HTN <35 years … A) All are indicators of early ESRD  B) None affects prognosis
opts: All four indicate ↑ chances of early ESRD
Only the age at diagnosis matters
questions.exp: Indicators of bad prognosis/↑ chances of early ESRD in ADPKD: black males, diagnosis before 30 years, haematuria at presentation, HTN <35 years and PKD1 truncating mutation. (Book p787)

questions.sec: ADPKD complications & renal stone types · p787
questions.q: All but one of the following increase the chance of early ESRD in ADPKD. Which is the odd one out?
questions.exp: PKD1 truncating mutation is an indicator of early ESRD; PKD2 mutations cause milder disease. The other listed indicators are black males, diagnosis before 30 years, haematuria at presentation and HTN <35 years. (Book p787)

questions.sec: ADPKD complications & renal stone types · p787
questions.q: In ADPKD, which single investigation is described as the strongest predictor of renal function decline?
opts: Kidney and cyst volume on MRI
questions.exp: Kidney and cyst volume on MRI is the strongest predictor for renal function decline; if within normal limits, chances of ESRD are less. (Book p787)

questions.sec: ADPKD complications & renal stone types · p787
questions.q: If kidney and cyst volume on MRI are within normal limits in ADPKD, the chances of ESRD are less.
opts: False — MRI volume does not correlate with outcome
False — a normal MRI volume worsens prognosis
True, but only in PKD2 disease
questions.exp: Kidney and cyst volume on MRI: strongest predictor for renal function decline; if within normal limits, chances of ESRD are less. (Book p787)

questions.sec: ADPKD complications & renal stone types · p787
questions.q: Match the ADPKD complication with its description — 1) Cyst hemorrhage  2) Cyst infection  3) Renal stones  4) Cyst rupture … A) Can be caused by blunt trauma to the abdomen (rare)  B) Commonest organism E. coli  C) Uric acid > calcium oxalate  D) Can cause haematuria
questions.exp: ADPKD complications: cyst haemorrhage can cause haematuria; cyst infection with E. coli as the commonest organism; renal stones uric acid > calcium oxalate; and cyst rupture (rare) from blunt abdominal trauma. (Book p787)

questions.sec: ADPKD complications & renal stone types · p787
questions.q: The commonest organism causing cyst infection in ADPKD is:
questions.exp: Cyst infection in ADPKD: the commonest organism is E. coli. (Book p787)

questions.sec: ADPKD complications & renal stone types · p787
questions.q: In ADPKD, uric acid stones are commoner than calcium oxalate stones.
opts: True — renal stones are uric acid > calcium oxalate
False — calcium oxalate stones are commoner
False — ADPKD patients never form stones
questions.exp: Renal stones in ADPKD: uric acid > calcium oxalate — unlike the general population, where calcium oxalate dominates. (Book p787)

questions.sec: ADPKD complications & renal stone types · p787
questions.q: A man with ADPKD develops sudden loin pain after a bicycle handlebar injury to the abdomen. Which rare complication fits?
questions.exp: Cyst rupture (rare) in ADPKD can be caused by blunt trauma to the abdomen. (Book p787)

questions.sec: ADPKD complications & renal stone types · p787
questions.q: Match the complications that present with abdominal pain — 1) Cyst hemorrhage and cyst infection  2) Renal stones and cyst rupture … A) All present with abdominal pain  B) None presents with abdominal pain
opts: All four present with abdominal pain
Only cyst infection presents with pain
Only renal stones present with pain
questions.exp: The brace in the book groups cyst haemorrhage, cyst infection, renal stones and cyst rupture together as presenting with abdominal pain. (Book p787)

questions.sec: ADPKD complications & renal stone types · p787
questions.q: Which cardiac abnormality is described in ADPKD, and why?
opts: Biventricular diastolic dysfunction — due to hypertension
Dilated cardiomyopathy — due to uraemic toxins alone
Constrictive pericarditis — due to uraemic pericarditis
Infective endocarditis — due to cyst infection
questions.exp: Biventricular diastolic dysfunction in ADPKD occurs due to hypertension (polycystin in vascular smooth muscle). (Book p787)

questions.sec: ADPKD complications & renal stone types · p787
questions.q: Match the commonest renal stone type with its setting — 1) General population  2) Renal tubular acidosis  3) ADPKD … A) Uric acid  B) Calcium oxalate  C) Calcium phosphate
questions.exp: Note on the commonest stone type in the kidney: generally calcium oxalate; in renal tubular acidosis calcium phosphate; in ADPKD uric acid. (Book p787)

questions.sec: ADPKD complications & renal stone types · p787
questions.q: Fill up: In renal tubular acidosis, the commonest renal stone is calcium ______.
questions.exp: Note: m/c stone in kidney — generally calcium oxalate; in RTA calcium phosphate; in ADPKD uric acid. (Book p787)

questions.sec: ADPKD management: investigations & treatment · p788
questions.q: Which statement about investigations in ADPKD is correct?
opts: RFT is normal, USG is the investigation of choice, and MRI evaluates the risk for ESRD
RFT is always raised with USG being only supportive
MRI is the investigation of choice for diagnosis, USG for risk
CT scan is the investigation of choice for diagnosis
questions.exp: ADPKD investigations: RFT normal; USG the IOC; MRI to evaluate the risk for ESRD; CT scan and CT urography for renal stones; FDG PET to find the source of infection in cyst infection. (Book p788)

questions.sec: ADPKD management: investigations & treatment · p788
questions.q: A 34-year-old with a family history of ADPKD has no cysts on ultrasound. Which investigation confirms that he can safely donate a kidney?
opts: MRI — more than 30 years old with not even one cyst on MRI means he can donate a kidney
Repeat ultrasound after 6 months to look for newly appearing renal cysts
CT urography showing both kidneys and the collecting systems clearly
Genetic testing of the PKD3 locus to exclude an inherited ADPKD mutation
questions.exp: Criteria to rule out ADPKD if family history is present but USG shows no cysts: >30 years with not even one cyst on MRI — such a person can donate a kidney. (Book p788)

questions.sec: ADPKD management: investigations & treatment · p788
questions.q: Match each ADPKD investigation with its purpose — 1) MRI  2) CT scan and CT urography  3) FDG PET scan … A) To find the source of infection (cyst infection)  B) To evaluate risk for ESRD  C) Renal stones
questions.exp: MRI evaluates risk for ESRD; CT scan and CT urography evaluate renal stones; FDG PET scan finds the source of infection in cyst infection. (Book p788)

questions.sec: ADPKD management: investigations & treatment · p788
questions.q: A patient with ADPKD and fever with loin pain is suspected to have cyst infection; blood cultures are negative. Which investigation is used to localise the source of infection?
questions.exp: FDG PET scan is used 'to find source of infection'—cyst infection in ADPKD. (Book p788)

questions.sec: ADPKD management: investigations & treatment · p788
questions.q: The rationale behind reducing osmolality in the treatment of ADPKD is:
opts: To reduce ADH, since cystic growth depends on ADH
To reduce blood pressure by natriuresis
To prevent hyperkalaemia from renin excess
To reduce the risk of hepatic cysts
questions.exp: Treatment of ADPKD begins with ↓osmolality to reduce ADH, because cystic growth depends on ADH. (Book p788)

questions.sec: ADPKD management: investigations & treatment · p788
questions.q: The daily fluid intake advised to lower osmolality in ADPKD is:
questions.exp: ↓Osmolality in ADPKD: ↑fluid intake 4–5 L/day, along with tolvaptan (DOC). (Book p788)

questions.sec: ADPKD management: investigations & treatment · p788
questions.q: The drug of choice in the treatment of ADPKD, and its class, are:
opts: Tolvaptan — an oral V₂ antagonist, 15 mg at night, monitoring LFT
Vaptan — an oral V₁ agonist, 30 mg in the morning
Everolimus — used as the drug of choice
questions.exp: Tolvaptan is the DOC in ADPKD: oral V₂ antagonist, 15 mg at night with LFT monitoring. Somatostatin analogues and everolimus are novel therapies. (Book p788)

questions.sec: ADPKD management: investigations & treatment · p788
questions.q: A patient with ADPKD is started on the drug of choice for cyst growth. Which baseline and follow-up monitoring is required?
opts: Liver function tests, since tolvaptan is an oral V₂ antagonist given at 15 mg at night
Serum amylase, since tolvaptan causes pancreatitis
ECG for QT prolongation, with 40 mg twice daily dosing
questions.exp: Tolvaptan (oral V₂ antagonist, 15 mg at night) requires monitoring of LFT. (Book p788)

questions.sec: ADPKD management: investigations & treatment · p788
questions.q: Match the drug category with the agent — 1) DOC for cyst growth  2) Novel therapies … A) Somatostatin analogues, everolimus  B) Tolvaptan
questions.exp: Tolvaptan is the DOC; novel therapies are somatostatin analogues and everolimus. (Book p788)

questions.sec: ADPKD management: investigations & treatment · p788
questions.q: In the ADPKD treatment section, tight BP control means a target of:
questions.exp: Tight BP control in ADPKD: SBP 95–110/DBP 60–75 mmHg using an ACE inhibitor or ARB. (Book p788)

questions.sec: ADPKD management: investigations & treatment · p788
questions.q: The antihypertensive classes specified for tight BP control in ADPKD are:
opts: Calcium channel blocker or beta blocker
Alpha blocker or centrally acting agent
questions.exp: Tight BP control (SBP 95–110/DBP 60–75 mmHg) in ADPKD is achieved with an ACE inhibitor or ARB. (Book p788)

questions.sec: ADPKD management: investigations & treatment · p788
questions.q: All but one of the following are part of the treatment or prevention plan in ADPKD. Which is the odd one out?
questions.exp: Treatment of ADPKD: ↓osmolality with fluids and tolvaptan, tight BP control with ACEi/ARB, novel therapies (somatostatin analogues, everolimus) and potassium citrate; steroids have no role. (Book p788)

questions.sec: ADPKD management: investigations & treatment · p788
questions.q: Which three measures are listed under prevention of complications in ADPKD?
opts: Watch for abdominal pain, avoid blunt trauma to prevent rupture, and potassium citrate to alkalinise urine and prevent stones
Avoid fluids, use NSAIDs for pain control, and start dialysis early in every patient
Prophylactic nephrectomy, lifelong prophylactic antibiotics, and strict bed rest at home
Vaccination against streptococci, statins for cholesterol control, and daily aspirin
questions.exp: Prevention of complications in ADPKD: watch out for abdominal pain; avoid blunt trauma (to prevent rupture); potassium citrate for alkalinisation of urine (to prevent renal stones). (Book p788)

questions.sec: ADPKD management: investigations & treatment · p788
questions.q: Fill up: In ADPKD, potassium citrate is given to ______ the urine and prevent renal stones.
questions.exp: Prevention of complications in ADPKD: potassium citrate causes alkalinisation of the urine to prevent renal stones. (Book p788)

questions.sec: ADPKD management: investigations & treatment · p788
questions.q: An ADPKD patient who plays contact sports asks about precautions. The correct advice from the prevention list is:
opts: Avoid blunt trauma to the abdomen to prevent cyst rupture, and report abdominal pain early
Continue all activities because rupture never occurs
Take NSAIDs before activity to prevent pain
questions.exp: Prevention list: watch out for abdominal pain and avoid blunt trauma (to prevent rupture of cysts). (Book p788)

questions.sec: ADPKD: cyst infection treatment & ESRD/nephrectomy · p788
questions.q: The antibiotics that penetrate cysts in ADPKD are remembered as CCC, namely:
questions.exp: Antibiotics that penetrate cysts (CCC): ciprofloxacin, cotrimoxazole and carbapenems — used for cyst infection. (Book p788)

questions.sec: ADPKD: cyst infection treatment & ESRD/nephrectomy · p788
questions.q: A patient with ADPKD and cyst infection requires antibiotics. Which set is appropriate?
questions.exp: Cyst-penetrating antibiotics in ADPKD are ciprofloxacin, cotrimoxazole and carbapenems (CCC). (Book p788)

questions.sec: ADPKD: cyst infection treatment & ESRD/nephrectomy · p788
questions.q: In ADPKD, renal transplantation reverses the extrarenal associations such as liver cysts.
opts: False — extrarenal associations cannot be reversed
True — transplantation cures the liver cysts
True, but only for colonic diverticula
False — renal transplantation is contraindicated in ADPKD
questions.exp: For ESRD (CKD) in ADPKD renal transplant is done, but extrarenal associations cannot be reversed — liver cysts, colonic diverticulum, saccular aneurysm, mitral valve prolapse, aortic root dilatation and hernias persist. (Book p788)

questions.sec: ADPKD: cyst infection treatment & ESRD/nephrectomy · p788
questions.q: Match the extrarenal association of ADPKD with the description given — 1) Liver cysts  2) Colonic diverticulum  3) Saccular aneurysm of anterior circulation … A) Significant if >10 mm  B) The commonest extrarenal association  C) A listed extrarenal association
questions.exp: Extrarenal associations of ADPKD: liver cysts (m/c); colonic diverticulum; saccular aneurysm of the anterior circulation (>10 mm is significant); mitral valve prolapse; AR/aortic root dilatation; abdominal wall/inguinal hernia. (Book p788)

questions.sec: ADPKD: cyst infection treatment & ESRD/nephrectomy · p788
questions.q: A saccular aneurysm of the anterior circulation in ADPKD is considered significant when it exceeds:
questions.exp: Saccular aneurysm of anterior circulation in ADPKD: >10 mm is significant. (Book p788)

questions.sec: ADPKD: cyst infection treatment & ESRD/nephrectomy · p788
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT listed as an extrarenal association of ADPKD?
questions.exp: Congenital hepatic fibrosis/Caroli's syndrome belongs to ARPKD (biliary duct involvement); ADPKD has liver cysts, colonic diverticulum, saccular aneurysm, mitral valve prolapse, aortic root dilatation and hernias. (Book p788)

questions.sec: ADPKD (contd): nephrectomy indications, brain note & ARPKD · p789
questions.q: Match the remaining extrarenal associations of ADPKD — 1) Cardiac valve  2) Aorta  3) Abdominal wall … A) Aortic root dilatation  B) Mitral valve prolapse  C) Inguinal hernia
questions.exp: Extrarenal associations continued: mitral valve prolapse (d), AR/aortic root dilatation (e), and abdominal wall/inguinal hernia (f). (Book p789)

questions.sec: ADPKD (contd): nephrectomy indications, brain note & ARPKD · p789
questions.q: Which of the following is the correct indication for pre-transplant nephrectomy in ADPKD?
opts: Uncontrolled hypertension, infection, obstruction and bleeding
A single previous episode of cyst haemorrhage
questions.exp: Indications for pre-transplant nephrectomy: (a) infection, (b) obstruction (no space for the transplanted kidney), (c) bleeding, (d) uncontrolled hypertension. (Book p789)

questions.sec: ADPKD (contd): nephrectomy indications, brain note & ARPKD · p789
questions.q: A patient with ADPKD and massively enlarged kidneys is being prepared for transplantation. Nephrectomy is indicated for the specific reason that:
opts: There is no space for the transplanted kidney (obstruction)
The kidneys contain more than 5% nephrons involved
Pre-transplant nephrectomy is mandatory in all ADPKD
Liver cysts will not be reversed otherwise
questions.exp: Pre-transplant nephrectomy indications include obstruction — no space for the transplanted kidney — along with infection, bleeding and uncontrolled hypertension. (Book p789)

questions.sec: ADPKD (contd): nephrectomy indications, brain note & ARPKD · p789
questions.q: In ADPKD the brain has no cysts.
opts: False — brain cysts are the hallmark of ADPKD
False — brain cysts occur in 10% of patients
questions.exp: Note: brain has no cysts in ADPKD, although saccular aneurysms of the anterior circulation (Berry aneurysms) can occur. (Book p789)

questions.sec: ADPKD (contd): nephrectomy indications, brain note & ARPKD · p789
questions.q: ARPKD is:
opts: Autosomal recessive and can be diagnosed in utero as small cysts in the medulla
Autosomal dominant and usually presents in middle age
X-linked and presents with haematuria in boys
Acquired and seen in adults with recurrent stones
questions.exp: ARPKD: autosomal recessive, and it can be diagnosed in utero (small cysts in the medulla). (Book p789)

questions.sec: ADPKD (contd): nephrectomy indications, brain note & ARPKD · p789
questions.q: Fill up: In ARPKD the gene defect is on chromosome 6: ______, which forms the fibrocystin–polyductin complex.
questions.exp: ARPKD gene defect: on chromosome 6 — PKHD1 → fibrocystin–polyductin complex, whose defect affects the cilia/centrosome complex. (Book p789)

questions.sec: ADPKD (contd): nephrectomy indications, brain note & ARPKD · p789
questions.q: Complete the ARPKD flowchart showing which ducts are affected and the resulting lesions — 1) Collecting duct  2) Biliary duct … A) Congenital hepatic fibrosis/Caroli's syndrome/biliary ectasia  B) Medullary cyst
questions.exp: ARPKD flowchart: defect of the fibrocystin-polyductin complex affects the cilia/centrosome complex, which is seen in the collecting duct (leading to medullary cyst) and biliary duct (leading to congenital hepatic fibrosis/Caroli's syndrome/biliary ectasia). (Book p789)

questions.sec: ADPKD (contd): nephrectomy indications, brain note & ARPKD · p789
questions.q: A neonate with ARPKD has hepatosplenomegaly and portal hypertension. The underlying lesion is:
opts: Congenital hepatic fibrosis with biliary ectasia from biliary duct involvement
Hepatic vein thrombosis from a hypercoagulable state in the neonatal period
Viral hepatitis acquired in utero and progressing to neonatal cirrhosis
Glycogen storage disease with massive hepatic glycogen deposition
questions.exp: ARPKD: the biliary duct branch of the fibrocystin defect gives congenital hepatic fibrosis (Caroli's syndrome/biliary ectasia), which produces portal hypertension. (Book p789)

questions.sec: ADPKD (contd): nephrectomy indications, brain note & ARPKD · p789
questions.q: What percentage of ARPKD babies with pulmonary hypoplasia die within 1 year?
questions.exp: Complications of ARPKD: pulmonary hypoplasia → 70% die within 1 year (major cause of death at birth). (Book p789)

questions.sec: ADPKD (contd): nephrectomy indications, brain note & ARPKD · p789
questions.q: Pulmonary hypoplasia is the major cause of death at birth in ARPKD.
opts: False — portal hypertension is the commonest cause of neonatal death
False — ESRD causes 70% of neonatal deaths
questions.exp: ARPKD: pulmonary hypoplasia causes 70% of deaths within 1 year and is the major cause of death at birth. (Book p789)

questions.sec: ADPKD (contd): nephrectomy indications, brain note & ARPKD · p789
questions.q: Match the ARPKD complication with the age of death and its cause — 1) Pulmonary hypoplasia  2) Portal hypertension (Caroli syndrome)  3) ESRD … A) Very rare; renal failure  B) 30% die at adolescence  C) 70% die within 1 year
questions.exp: ARPKD complications: pulmonary hypoplasia — 70% die within 1 year (major cause of death at birth); portal hypertension from Caroli syndrome — remaining 30% die at adolescence; ESRD is very rare but causes renal failure. (Book p789)

questions.sec: ADPKD (contd): nephrectomy indications, brain note & ARPKD · p789
questions.q: All but one of the following are complications listed for ARPKD. Which is the odd one out?
questions.exp: ARPKD complications listed are pulmonary hypoplasia, portal hypertension (Caroli syndrome) and rarely ESRD; cyst infection is an ADPKD complication. (Book p789)

questions.sec: ARPKD: ultrasound findings · p789
questions.q: Match the ARPKD ultrasound signs — 1) Echogenicity of the medulla  2) Corticomedullary differentiation … A) Lost  B) Hyperechoic
questions.exp: USG in ARPKD: hyperechoic medulla with loss of corticomedullary differentiation. (Book p789)

questions.sec: ARPKD: ultrasound findings · p789
questions.q: The two ultrasound findings described in ARPKD are:
opts: Hyperechoic medulla and loss of corticomedullary differentiation
Hypoechoic medulla and preserved corticomedullary differentiation
Multiple cortical cysts with normal medulla
questions.exp: Investigation in ARPKD (USG): hyperechoic medulla and loss of corticomedullary differentiation, consistent with small medullary cysts. (Book p789)

questions.sec: ARPKD: ultrasound findings · p789
questions.q: An antenatal ultrasound at 30 weeks shows bilaterally enlarged echogenic kidneys with small medullary cysts and no corticomedullary differentiation, plus oligohydramnios. Which diagnosis fits?
questions.exp: ARPKD is autosomal recessive and can be diagnosed in utero with small cysts in the medulla; USG shows hyperechoic medulla with loss of corticomedullary differentiation. (Book p789)

questions.sec: ARPKD: ultrasound findings · p789
questions.q: The cut section of the kidney in ARPKD shows small cysts in the medulla rather than the large cysts typical of ADPKD.
opts: False — ARPKD shows large cortical cysts
False — ARPKD shows a single cyst
questions.exp: ARPKD can be diagnosed in utero with small cysts in the medulla (figure 'ARPKD: cut section of kidney'), unlike ADPKD's multiple large cysts. (Book p789)

questions.sec: ARPKD: ultrasound findings · p789
questions.q: A neonate with ARPKD is in respiratory distress with a small chest. The underlying mechanism and outcome described are:
opts: Pulmonary hypoplasia from oligohydramnios — 70% die within 1 year
Pneumothorax from mechanical ventilation — usually survives
questions.exp: ARPKD with pulmonary hypoplasia: 70% succumb to death within 1 year, the major cause of death at birth. (Book p789)

questions.sec: Juvenile nephronophthisis vs MCDK (ADTKD) table · p790

questions.q: In MCDK (ADTKD), ESRD typically develops by:
questions.exp: MCDK: adults, starts by 20–25 years with ESRD by 40–50 years. (Book p790)

questions.exp: NPHP1 on chr 2 → nephrocystin; defect affects the cilia/centrosome complex in juvenile nephronophthisis. (Book p790)

questions.sec: Juvenile nephronophthisis vs MCDK (ADTKD) table · p790

questions.exp: Pathology of juvenile nephronophthisis: tubular basement membrane irregularity; tubular atrophy → CKD (CTID with shrunken kidney); cysts few; interstitial infiltration with fibrosis. (Book p790)

questions.sec: Juvenile nephronophthisis vs MCDK (ADTKD) table · p790

questions.sec: Juvenile nephronophthisis vs MCDK (ADTKD) table · p790

questions.exp: Pathology of juvenile nephronophthisis: cysts are few (in contrast to the multiple cysts of ADPKD/ARPKD). (Book p790)

questions.exp: Clinical features of juvenile nephronophthisis: salt wasting, polyuria and failure to thrive. (Book p790)

questions.exp: MCDK clinical features: similar to juvenile nephronophthisis except for failure to thrive, which is absent because growth is complete. (Book p790)

MCDK typically presents with macroscopic haematuria, renal stones and recurrent UTI
questions.exp: MCDK (ADTKD) clinical features resemble JN but without failure to thrive, because growth is complete in adults. (Book p790)

False — rickets-like changes are equally present in JN and in MCDK

units.title: Ciliopathy overview: cilia function and the four types
units.guide: Ciliopathies are hereditary cystic disorders of the kidney in which a ciliary defect strips the tubular epithelium of its differentiated phenotype; polycystin regulates this function. The TYPES flowchart gives four entities: ADPKD, ARPKD, juvenile nephronophthisis and MCDK.

units.title: ADPKD: genes, Ravinson's criteria, renal and systemic features
units.guide: ADPKD is autosomal dominant with variable expression, 10% spontaneous mutations, multiple bilateral cysts as the hallmark and only 5% of nephrons involved. PKD1 (Chr16p, 85%, polycystin 1), PKD2 (Chr4q, 15%, polycystin 2, milder), PKD3 (GANA B); polycystin in vascular smooth muscle explains HTN. Ravinson's USG criteria by age band; asymptomatic presentation, abdominal discomfort at 30–40, nocturia/polyuria from impaired concentrating capacity, least anaemia of CKD, and the complications with their prognosis indicators and stone types.

units.title: ADPKD management, cyst infection and transplant decisions
units.guide: Investigations (normal RFT, USG the IOC, MRI for ESRD risk, CT/CT urography for stones, FDG PET for cyst infection) and the MRI rule for a family member wanting to donate. Treatment lowers osmolality to reduce ADH (fluids 4–5 L/day, tolvaptan 15 mg at night with LFT monitoring), tight BP control (SBP 95–110/DBP 60–75 with ACEi/ARB), novel therapies, prevention measures, CCC antibiotics for cyst infection, transplant with irreversible extrarenal associations, and the four indications for pre-transplant nephrectomy. The brain has no cysts.

units.title: ARPKD: gene flowchart, complications and ultrasound
units.guide: ARPKD is autosomal recessive, diagnosable in utero with small medullary cysts. PKHD1 on chromosome 6 makes the fibrocystin-polyductin complex; its defect affects the cilia/centrosome complex in the collecting duct (medullary cyst) and biliary duct (congenital hepatic fibrosis/Caroli/biliary ectasia). Pulmonary hypoplasia kills 70% within a year, portal hypertension the remaining 30% at adolescence, ESRD rarely. USG: hyperechoic medulla with loss of corticomedullary differentiation.

units.title: Juvenile nephronophthisis vs MCDK (ADTKD)
units.guide: The side-by-side table: AR versus AD; children from 5–7 years to ESRD by 13 years versus adults from 20–25 years to ESRD by 40–50 years; NPHP1 (chr 2, nephrocystin) versus MCDK1 (chr 1) and MCDK2 (chr 16, uromodulin); pathology of tubular basement membrane irregularity, tubular atrophy and interstitial fibrosis; clinical features with rickets-like changes; extrarenal syndromes Senior Loken, Cogan, Joubert with situs inversus; and absent recurrence after transplant in both.

units.title: ADPKD vs ARPKD vs juvenile nephronophthisis and medullary sponge kidney
units.guide: The three-way comparison table across age, kidney size, cysts, cyst infection, BP, nephrocalcinosis, CNS and liver manifestations and chromosomes. Then medullary sponge kidney — not a ciliopathy, acquired, 30–50 years, F > M in India, no CKD risk — with its pathogenesis (terminal collecting duct malformation), triad, associations (incomplete distal RTA in 50%), investigations (paintbrush/bouquet on excretory urography) and treatment, ending with the medullary versus cortical nephrocalcinosis lists and the oxalosis exception.
